latest_release.body:
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jnunemaker/httparty/compare/v0.24.3...v0.24.4

## Deprecations

HTTParty 0.25 will stop adding a trailing slash to an empty (`""`), query-only (`"?a=1"`) or fragment-only (`"#top"`) request path. Today, `get("")` against `base_uri "https://example.com/api/articles"` requests `/api/articles/`. In 0.25 it will request `/api/articles`, which matches RFC 3986 and what curl, Faraday, axios and other HTTP clients do. (#742, #898, #900)

This release changes no URLs. It prints a `[DEPRECATION]` warning to stderr, once per request, for each request whose URL will change in 0.25:

```
[DEPRECATION] HTTParty added a trailing slash to the request path (/api/articles/) because the path passed to the request was empty. ...
```

The warning shows only the path, never the full URL, so credentials or query values in your `base_uri` are not printed.

**To keep the trailing slash** in 0.25, pass `"/"` as the path. It requests the same URL in both versions and silences the warning:

```ruby
get("/") # https://example.com/api/articles/ in 0.24 and 0.25
```

**If you want the 0.25 behavior**, no change is needed and the warning goes away when you upgrade. To get it now and silence the warning, pass a `URI` object, which HTTParty already uses as given:

```ruby
get(URI("")) # https://example.com/api/articles in 0.24 and 0.25
```

There is no warning when nothing will change: non-empty paths, `get("/")`, a `base_uri` without a path, absolute URLs, the Addressable adapter, and redirects.

## Bug Fixes

### Requests

- The `headers:` option and the `cookies` class method accept any object that responds to `to_hash`, as documented. Before, such objects raised `NoMethodError` or `RuntimeError`. (#899)
- Callable header values work with any object that responds to `call`, not only procs and lambdas. (#897)
- Multipart bodies accept hash-like objects that respond to `to_hash`. (#894)
- Arrays inside inherited options, such as `default_params tags: ["one"]`, are copied for each subclass, so changing them in one class no longer changes them in its parent or sibling classes. (#896)
- `head` no longer modifies the options hash you pass to it. (#884)
- `webcal://` requests keep their query string, including the `query:` option. (#859)

### Responses

- A `parsed_response` of `false` or `nil` is cached, so the parser runs once instead of on every call. (#893)
- Responses with a capitalized content type, such as `Application/JSON`, are parsed. (#877)
- Responses can be marshaled when their request has a proc option or a `debug_output` stream. (#885)

### Streaming uploads

- Streamed multipart reads return no more than the requested number of bytes. (#895)
- Files are rewound after a streamed upload, so they can be read or sent again. (#882)

### Cookies and digest auth

- Following a redirect no longer sends `Max-Age` back as a cookie. (#878)
- Digest auth sends each cookie as `name=value` only, without attributes like `Path` or `HttpOnly`. (#888)
- A digest auth cookie and your own `Cookie` header are joined with `; ` in one header. Before they were joined with a comma, so servers read them as a single cookie and the digest session was lost. (#889)
- Digest auth answers a challenge that offers several `qop` values with just one. (#886)
- When digest auth retries a request, your streaming block now receives the authenticated response. Before, the retry ran without your block. (#883)

### Logging and CLI

- The curl log format no longer raises `Encoding::CompatibilityError` on a binary response body, and it logs bodies in other charsets, such as Latin-1, as readable UTF-8. (#848, #873, thanks @harissmansoor)
- The curl log format handles a string `query:` option instead of raising. (#887)
- `Logger.add_formatter` treats string and symbol names the same, so a string name can no longer silently replace a built-in formatter like `:curl`. (#869)
- `bin/httparty` keeps every colon after the first in `--header` values and `--user

detail.readme:
# httparty

[![CI](https://github.com/jnunemaker/httparty/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jnunemaker/httparty/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Makes http fun again! Ain't no party like a httparty, because a httparty don't stop.

## Install

```
gem install httparty
```

## Requirements

- Ruby 2.7.0 or higher
- You like to party!

## Examples

```ruby
# Use the class methods to get down to business quickly
response = HTTParty.get('https://api.stackexchange.com/2.2/questions?site=stackoverflow')

puts response.body, response.code, response.message, response.headers.inspect

# Or wrap things up in your own class
class StackExchange
  include HTTParty
  base_uri 'api.stackexchange.com'

  def initialize(service, page)
    @options = { query: { site: service, page: page } }
  end

  def questions
    self.class.get("/2.2/questions", @options)
  end

  def users
    self.class.get("/2.2/users", @options)
  end
end

stack_exchange = StackExchange.new("stackoverflow", 1)
puts stack_exchange.questions
puts stack_exchange.users
```

See the [examples directory](http://github.com/jnunemaker/httparty/tree/main/examples) for even more goodies.

## Command Line Interface

httparty also includes the executable `httparty` which can be
used to query web services and examine the resulting output. By default
it will output the response as a pretty-printed Ruby object (useful for
grokking the structure of output). This can also be overridden to output
formatted XML or JSON. Execute `httparty --help` for all the
options. Below is an example of how easy it is.

```
httparty "https://api.stackexchange.com/2.2/questions?site=stackoverflow"
```

## Help and Docs

- [Docs](https://github.com/jnunemaker/httparty/tree/main/docs)
- https://github.com/jnunemaker/httparty/discussions
- https://www.rubydoc.info/github/jnunemaker/httparty

## Contributing

- Fork the project.
- Run `bundle`
- Run `bundle exec rake`
- Make your feature addition or bug fix.
- Add tests for it. This is important so I don't break it in a future version unintentionally.
- Run `bundle exec rake` (No, REALLY :))
- Commit, do not mess with rakefile, version, or history. (if you want to have your own version, that is fine but bump version in a commit by itself in another branch so I can ignore when I pull)
- Send me a pull request. Bonus points for topic branches.
